metadata.title: Biodiversity increases the resistance of ecosystem productivity to climate extremes

summary: Nature study demonstrating that higher species richness provides critical ecosystem resistance and buffers productivity collapses during severe drought.

sections.text: Ecosystems with higher plant species richness sustain productivity during climate extremes, including severe drought. Monocultures consistently experience severe biomass loss during water stress, whereas diverse plant communities maintain below-ground microbial associations and root niche differentiation.

Low diversity plant stands show half the resistance of high diversity stands during precipitation anomalies, demonstrating that biodiversity is a functional prerequisite for climate resilience in rainfed landscapes.
